threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it’s weird when a pub runs out of drink before closing time. Welcome to Dalston, where ‘last orders’ can mean anything.
Caught the 196 last night; three guys had a full-on debate about the best chicken shops in Brixton. Turns out it’s a real rivalry.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade on the sidewalk, while a street musician played the accordion nearby. Pure Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find spontaneous street parties where the DJ is just a guy with a portable speaker, and everyone’s welcome to join in.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to dodge the BART delays like it's a game of Frogger, especially on Fridays after 5.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo, complete with top hat, hop off the bus at 19th and Mission—only in SF. Muni brings out the best and weirdest in us.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to the plaça, but they miss the real charm down the side streets where the old grocers still barter and gossip over coffee.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they still carry a mapa de Barcelona; locals just pull out Google Maps on their phones without a second thought.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think saying 'hello' to strangers on the street is normal. Here, it's like you're trying to start a conversation about the Tube strikes.
Caught the 333 last night. A guy in a dinosaur onesie was arguing with a pigeon for a whole stop. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids turning an empty lot into a pop-up skate park, complete with makeshift ramps and a boom box blaring techno.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you find a Kiez where a techno party can end at sunrise and the local bakery opens up just in time for breakfast rolls. It's a wild rhythm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their eye roll at tourists stopping in the crosswalk to snap pics of the murals, completely blocking the flow.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 38 Geary doing a full magic show for the packed bus. People were laughing, forgetting about the delays. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the tickets to Sagrada Família go fast, but locals know the true secret is just skipping the crowded Gaudí spots altogether.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their bewilderment at those tiny cafes trying to charge a euro for your 'un llaç de cafè' instead of just a regular coffee.
